source.title: UV Unwrapping in Blender (Full Beginner Tutorial) #b3d
source.creator: CG Boost

analysis.study_scope: Torus UV unwrapping, distortion visualization, rectification using Follow Active Quads and UV Toolkit, multi-object UV scale normalization, and island packing.

episodes.problem: Unwrapping a closed torus shape causes severe ring distortion with a single seam.
episodes.observed_fact: A single transverse seam unfolds the torus into a pinched, circular ring island in the UV Editor.
episodes.instructor_claim: A torus is an endless cylinder connected to itself, requiring two seams to lay flat.
episodes.interpretation: A single cut breaks the longitudinal loop but leaves the radial perimeter closed.
episodes.hypothesis: Adding an inner longitudinal perimeter seam allows the mesh to unfold into a strip.
episodes.reference_evidence: Marking an inner loop seam unwraps the torus into a continuous ribbon.
episodes.modeling_decision: Mark a second seam along the inner circumference loop.
episodes.visible_action: Selects inner edge loop with Alt+Click and selects Mark Seam.
episodes.spoken_reason: Cutting along the inner length opens the ring into a strip.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: UV island unfolds into a rectangular ribbon shape instead of a pinched circular loop.
episodes.failure: Single seam unwrapping produced extreme circular warping.
episodes.alternatives: Cutting along the outer perimeter loop.
episodes.transferable_principle: Toroidal geometries require two perpendicular seams (one cross-sectional, one longitudinal) to unfold flat.

episodes.problem: The unwrapped torus strip is bowed and has uneven face areas.
episodes.observed_fact: Outer perimeter 3D edges are longer than inner ones; enabling UV Stretch Area mode turns the center green and edges blue.
episodes.instructor_claim: Blender balances 3D edge proportions, resulting in curved UV boundaries and stretch.
episodes.interpretation: Conformal unwrapping maintains edge ratio differences, bowing the UV island.
episodes.hypothesis: UV Stretch overlay visually identifies area compression versus expansion.
episodes.reference_evidence: Enabling UV Stretch Area overlay shades the torus island in blue and green.
episodes.modeling_decision: Enable UV Stretch overlay set to Area mode.
episodes.visible_action: Opens Viewport Overlays in UV Editor, enables UV Stretch, and sets type to Area.
episodes.spoken_reason: Visualizes where texture stretching and compression occur.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Island displays color heatmap showing relative area distortion across quad rows.
episodes.failure: Manual visual check fails to pinpoint subtle area distortions.
episodes.transferable_principle: UV stretch overlays highlight geometric distortion caused by uneven mesh loop circumferences.

episodes.problem: Curved UV islands cause wavy texture lines along quad strips.
episodes.observed_fact: Aligning one quad face straight, selecting all faces, and running Follow Active Quads turns the island rectangular.
episodes.instructor_claim: Straightening a reference quad allows Follow Active Quads to align the rest of the mesh grid.
episodes.interpretation: Follow Active Quads copies orthogonal quad alignment across connected mesh faces.
episodes.hypothesis: Unstraightened active quads propagate shear across the entire island.
episodes.reference_evidence: Selecting an unaligned quad and running Follow Active Quads distorts the UV island diagonally.
episodes.modeling_decision: Straighten one active quad face before calling Follow Active Quads.
episodes.visible_action: Aligns active quad edges horizontally/vertically, selects all, and clicks Follow Active Quads.
episodes.spoken_reason: Ensures the algorithm propagates a clean, non-skewed rectangular grid.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Bowed UV island snaps into a straight, uniform rectangular grid.
episodes.failure: Running Follow Active Quads on an unaligned face sheared the UV grid.
episodes.correction: Undid operation, straightened reference face first, then re-ran algorithm.
episodes.alternatives: Manually pinning and aligning boundary vertex rows.
episodes.transferable_principle: Follow Active Quads requires an explicitly orthogonal reference quad to prevent grid shearing.

episodes.problem: Manually straightening multiple torus UV islands is slow.
episodes.observed_fact: Using UV Toolkit's Straighten UVs batch-rectifies multiple selected torus islands, but leaves scales mismatched.
episodes.instructor_claim: Add-ons automate multi-object quad straightening; Average Island Scale fixes texel discrepancies.
episodes.interpretation: Batch tools apply straightening per island, requiring post-process scale normalization.
episodes.hypothesis: Average Island Scale adjusts relative island sizes based on 3D surface area.
episodes.reference_evidence: Clicking Average Island Scale resizes all straightened islands to uniform texel density.
episodes.modeling_decision: Use UV Toolkit to batch-straighten UVs, then execute Average Island Scale.
episodes.visible_action: Enables UV Toolkit in Preferences, uses Straighten UVs in sidebar, then selects UV -> Average Island Scale.
episodes.spoken_reason: Automates repetitive multi-object unwrapping while maintaining equal texture scale.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: All UV islands become straight rectangular strips of identical texel scale.
episodes.failure: Batch straightening created unequal island scales across identical 3D objects.
episodes.correction: Executed Average Island Scale after batch straightening.
episodes.alternatives: Manually straightening each torus island individually.
episodes.transferable_principle: Automated batch UV processing requires texel scale normalization across objects afterwards.

episodes.problem: Straightened UV strips extend beyond texture bounds and overlap.
episodes.observed_fact: Pack Islands fits strips inside the 0-1 space; setting Margin to 0.01 adds visible spacing.
episodes.instructor_claim: Pack Islands arranges UVs inside the tile and margin prevents texture bleeding.
episodes.interpretation: Packing algorithms scale and position islands into [0,1] space with safety padding.
episodes.hypothesis: Setting zero margin causes texture bleeding between neighboring UV islands.
episodes.reference_evidence: Increasing margin parameter from 0.001 to 0.01 creates clear gaps between vertical strips.
episodes.modeling_decision: Apply Pack Islands with an explicit margin padding.
episodes.visible_action: Selects UV -> Pack Islands and inputs 0.01 into Margin field.
episodes.spoken_reason: Prevents adjacent islands from bleeding texture pixels into each other.
episodes.topology_surface_effect: Islands fit inside 0-1 texture bounds with clean separation gaps.
episodes.failure: Unpacked strips overflowed the UV tile boundaries.
episodes.correction: Executed Pack Islands with a 0.01 margin.
episodes.alternatives: Manually scaling and arranging UV strips inside the tile.
episodes.transferable_principle: Always pack UV islands with explicit margin padding to prevent texture bleeding across boundaries.
